# OpenCharm

> OpenCharm is an open-source body for the AI agent you already run: a face made of typed glyphs, a voice and one key. Today it lives at the top of your Mac or Windows screen as the desktop charm; next, on a small ESP32-S3 board you build yourself (about $32 of hardware). One agent at a time; the charm holds no API keys, and the microphone is open only while the key is held.

It works with any agent over ACP (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, goose, Hermes Agent, OpenClaw) or an OpenAI-compatible API; Claude Code is tested end to end. charmd, the charm daemon, runs next to the agent and handles pairing, the PIN and voice. The project sells and ships nothing and comes with no warranty.

Status: the desktop charm (macOS; Windows untested) and charmd work today, and the CLI is on npm (`opencharm`); the firmware port to the board is next.
